subject: Dedicated lane mapping and staggered activation options
messages:
From: Arielle Summers <arielle@lyraonehealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tony Delgado <tony@lyraonehealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@lyraonehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity — early sizing and activation cadence

Hi Michael / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our team (Tony + procurement copied) wants a concise set of options we can take to leadership this week. High level asks:
- Typical minimums you recommend for an initial production cluster (low-latency chat + moderate embedding throughput)
- Ramp schedule options that balance cost vs. latency risk (we may prefer a two-stage activation)
- Burst capabilities if we exceed baseline traffic for short periods

We have a firm timeline: pilot opens Jan 10, 2028; production target Feb 28, 2028. Leadership wants a formalized proposal before Dec 10.

Also, please include any documents or example activation plans and a short note on guaranteed SLAs for Dedicated lanes.

Thanks,
Arielle
Arielle Summers
VP Product, LyraOne Health
arielle@lyraonehealth.com

(Attachment: sample_requirements.xlsx)

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Arielle Summers <arielle@lyraonehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2027 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — early sizing and activation cadence

Arielle — thanks for the clear timeline. Below are three practical reservation options (short bullets so you can paste into a leadership note). I'll attach a short PDF with line-item cost for each option.

Option A — Pilot hybrid (cost-conscious):
- 8 nominal GPUs in a shared-dedicated pool (min-guarantee 4 GPUs during business hours)
- Ramp: 2 weeks warm + gradual activation over 3 weeks to reach 8 GPUs
- Bursting: can burst to an extra 4 GPUs for short periods (subject to capacity)
- Tradeoffs: lower base cost, higher variability in peak latency

Option B — Hybrid reserved (recommended for predictable latency):
- 16 GPUs reserved; min 12 GPUs for baseline traffic
- Ramp: 1-week warm, then immediate 50% capacity for first month, 100% by month 2
- Bursting: dedicated cold spare pool + short-term borrow from regional pool
- Tradeoffs: better P95 latency consistency, moderate cost

Option C — Full dedicated cluster (SLA-forward):
- 32 GPUs reserved with clustered failover in secondary region
- Ramp: staged activation (8 GPUs / week over 4 weeks) with warm caches preloaded
- Bursting: integrated burst lanes and priority routing for critical traffic
- Tradeoffs: highest cost, strongest latency guarantees and isolation

Notes:
- Min GPU lines reflect realistic warm-up behavior for KV cache and batching.
- We can add a short onboarding credit for the first 30 days to offset ramp inefficiency.

Next steps: I can send a versioned PDF (LyraOne_Dedicated_Options_v3.pdf) with cost per GPU-hour and a sample activation_plan.xlsx. Marissa / Grace — any tweaks on guarantees or activation timing?

Best,
Michael Grant
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: LyraOne_Dedicated_Options_v3.pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Arielle Summers <arielle@lyraonehealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2027 11:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — early sizing and activation cadence

Arielle / Michael — quick add from pricing & commercial:
- We can offer a one-time onboarding credit equal to 10% of the first-month committed spend for deals that sign a minimum 6-month Dedicated reservation.
- For Option B (16 GPUs) our suggested contractual minimum is a 6-month commit to keep unit economics predictable.
- DocuSign path ready; I can draft the commitment schedule and the ramp milestones so procurement has clear acceptance gates.

Suggested acceptance milestones for procurement:
1) Contract signed + PO received
2) Week 0 — baseline cluster provisioned (warm start begins)
3) Week 2 — 50% capacity validated under load test
4) Week 4 — 100% capacity live and SLA baseline validated

I will include the cost breakout CSV and a short schedule in the DocuSign envelope unless you prefer a separate purchase order flow.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Solutions & GTM, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: cost_breakdown_Q4_2027.csv)

From: Arielle Summers <arielle@lyraonehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Tony Delgado <tony@lyraonehealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@lyraonehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Dec 2027 08:51:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — early sizing and activation cadence

Thanks — a few clarifying questions before we present to the execs:
1) For Option B, can you guarantee cross-region failover within 15 minutes for critical endpoints? If not, what is typical RTO we should budget for?
2) When you say "burst" to an extra 4 GPUs, is pricing billed at on-demand GPU rate or a blended rate?
3) We need a short paragraph we can use in the memo on how warm caches and KV preloads are handled during staged activation.

Also looping Security briefly — do you have a short statement on data residency and whether logs/audit events for Dedicated lanes can be sent to our KMS?

Best,
Arielle

(Replying inline: sample_requirements.xlsx attached)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Arielle Summers <arielle@lyraonehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Dec 2027 09:13:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — early sizing and activation cadence

Arielle — short answers and an operational note you can paste into the memo:

1) Cross-region failover:
- We can enable automated failover to a warm standby cluster in a secondary region. Typical RTO for route convergence and cache warming is 10–30 minutes depending on model size and active KV cache. For your requested 15-minute SLA we recommend Option C with a pre-warmed standby and prioritized routing.

2) Burst pricing:
- Short bursts are billed at a blended burst rate (reserved customers get a discount on burst GPU-hours vs on-demand). We will include blended examples in the PDF.

3) Warm cache / KV preload paragraph (pasteable):
- "During staged activation, Redwood pre-warms model execution paths and preloads KV/prefix caches using a coordinated traffic replay. This reduces cold-start P95s substantially. Warm-up runs are executed within the reserved pool prior to user traffic and are validated with synthetic load tests."

Operational activation schedule (suggested, with dates):
- Week 0 (2028-01-03): Provision baseline reserved hardware and test control-plane integration
- Week 1 (2028-01-10): Warm-run 25% traffic replay and KV preload
- Week 2 (2028-01-17): 50% traffic validation and latency baseline testing
- Week 4 (2028-01-31): Full production cutover to reserved capacity

I've attached a short activation_plan.xlsx with the checklist and owner assignments. Security: we can support sending audit logs to your KMS-backed storage and set retention windows per your policy; I'll loop in security separately for the exact KMS workflow.

-Grace
Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
(Attachment: activation_plan.xlsx)
